Title: Diagnosis of test `testCompareTo_otherEnumType`

Details: The test `testCompareTo_otherEnumType` calls `ValuedColorEnum.BLUE.compareTo(ValuedLanguageEnum.ENGLISH)` and expects a `ClassCastException` to be thrown when comparing two different enum types. The test expects that comparing two different ValuedEnum subclasses will result in a runtime exception.

Examining the implementation of `ValuedEnum.compareTo(Object other)` shows that it simply performs a subtraction of the `iValue` field from the other object's `iValue` field after casting `other` to `ValuedEnum`:
```java
public int compareTo(Object other) {
    return iValue - ((ValuedEnum) other).iValue;
}
```
This cast is always successful if the `other` object is any subclass of `ValuedEnum`, regardless of whether it is the exact same enum type or not. So if `other` is a different subclass of `ValuedEnum` (like `ValuedLanguageEnum` when called on `ValuedColorEnum`), the cast does not fail, and the subtraction proceeds.

Because the subtraction proceeds and returns an int result, no `ClassCastException` is thrown during the `compareTo` call, contrary to the test expectation. As a result, the test immediately calls `fail()`, causing the test to fail.

Thus, the root cause is that `ValuedEnum.compareTo(Object other)` does not verify that the other object is of the exact same enum subclass prior to performing the comparison. It only casts to the base `ValuedEnum` class.

To fix this, `compareTo` should check the runtime type of `other` and throw `ClassCastException` if `other` is not the same subclass type, to match the test expectation of type-safety on `compareTo`.

Suggested methods to fix:
- org.apache.commons.lang.enums.ValuedEnum.compareTo(java.lang.Object)
